title: Daily Life - What Mood Are You In
audio: mp3/362. Daily Life - What Mood Are You In.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
My name is Marco.
My name is Catherine.
What's wrong Catherine?
I'm just a little down today.
You're having a, you're in the mood, you're not in the mood today?
segments.zh: 你有一个，你有心情，你今天没有心情？

segments.en: Is that what's going on?
segments.zh: 这就是正在发生的事情吗？

segments.en: I am not in the mood to record today.
Actually no, I am in the mood.
So we're talking about moods, feelings, emotions.
segments.zh: 所以我们谈论的是心情、感觉和情绪。

segments.en: This is today's podcast and we're going to be learning a lot of the names for different kinds of feelings.
segments.zh: 这是今天的播客，我们将学习很多不同感受的名称。

segments.en: That's right, so you're going to learn how to describe what mood you're in.
segments.zh: 没错，所以你将学习如何描述你的情绪。

segments.en: Maybe you're in a good mood, bad mood, etc.
segments.zh: 也许你心情好，心情不好等。

segments.en: So let's just jump into the dialogue and see what's going on.
segments.zh: 所以让我们跳进对话，看看发生了什么。

segments.en: Are you okay?
You seem a bit anxious.
Yeah, I'm okay.
I've been having a lot of mood swings lately.
segments.zh: 我最近情绪起伏特别大。

segments.en: I think it has to do with the pills my doctor prescribed that are causing chaos on my hormones.
segments.zh: 我想是医生开的药影响了激素，让我情绪乱了套。

segments.en: So you mean you feel ecstatic one minute and then blue the next?
segments.zh: 也就是说，你一会儿欣喜若狂，一会儿又闷闷不乐？

segments.en: Yeah, it's weird.
For example, just this morning I was feeling detached and lonely, even though there was really no reason to feel that way.
segments.zh: 就像今天早上，我无缘无故觉得跟周围格格不入，又很孤单。

segments.en: Well maybe your mood will swing positively and you will feel confident, brave and hopeful.
segments.zh: 也许你的情绪会往好的方向转，变得自信、勇敢、充满希望。

segments.en: I hope you're right.
Okay, lots of feelings.
So many feelings in fact that we're going to talk about the names of them in today's Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 事实上，我们将在今天的语言要点中谈论它们的名称。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
So on Language Takeaway, let's take a look at this adjective.
segments.zh: 所以在语言要点方面，让我们来看看这个形容词。

segments.en: You are feeling or you seem a little bit anxious.
segments.zh: 你感觉或者你看起来有点焦虑。

segments.en: Anxious.
He is anxious.
I feel anxious.
That's right.
Now this word means that you're feeling nervous or uneasy about something.
segments.zh: 现在这个词意味着你对某事感到紧张或不安。

segments.en: Normally when you feel anxious about something like a test, all you can think about is the test.
segments.zh: 通常，当您对测试之类的事情感到焦虑时，您所能想到的只是测试。

segments.en: Oh, will I fail?
What's going to happen?
Did I study enough?
You're worried.
So this is an anxious feeling.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种焦虑的感觉。

segments.en: That's right.
So if you're anxious, you're worried about something or you're nervous about something.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您感到焦虑，您会担心某事或对某事感到紧张。

segments.en: It could be about your job, interview, a test, etc.
segments.zh: 这可能是关于你的工作、面试、考试等。

segments.en: All right, so moving on now.
We're feeling anxious, but then we also feel a different type of excitement.
segments.zh: 我们感到焦虑，但随后我们也感到不同类型的兴奋。

segments.en: We are ecstatic.
All right.
So well, anxious is a bad feeling.
segments.zh: 好吧，焦虑是一种不好的感觉。

segments.en: Ecstatic is a really good feeling.
segments.zh: 欣喜若狂是一种非常好的感觉。

segments.en: Okay.
Okay, so I'm happy.
I'm really happy.
I'm ecstatic.
That's a really, really, really happy feeling.
segments.zh: 这是一种非常非常、非常快乐的感觉。

segments.en: Okay, so if you're ecstatic, it means you're very, very happy.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果你欣喜若狂，这意味着你非常非常高兴。

segments.en: So it's not a negative thing.
segments.zh: 所以这不是负面的事情。

segments.en: No.
So when I get a hundred percent on my test, I'm ecstatic.
segments.zh: 因此，当我在考试中获得百分之百时，我欣喜若狂。

segments.en: I'm really happy.
Okay.
Now basically the complete opposite of being ecstatic would be to feel or be blue.
segments.zh: 基本上，跟 ecstatic 完全相反的，就是 feel blue / be blue，也就是忧郁。

segments.en: Yeah.
It might seem a bit strange because blue is a color, as you know, B-L-U-E.
segments.zh: 这可能看起来有点奇怪，因为如你所知，蓝色是一种颜色，B-L-U-E。

segments.en: But when you're feeling blue, it means that you're feeling sad or down or upset.
segments.zh: 但当你 feel blue 时，意思是感到难过、低落或郁闷。

segments.en: You're depressed.
Yeah.
So maybe this is why you also have music, the blues, right?
segments.zh: 所以也许这就是为什么你也有音乐，布鲁斯，对吧？

segments.en: The blues.
He's got the blues.
segments.zh: 他心情很低落；他很忧郁。

segments.en: That means he's sad about something, usually a woman.
segments.zh: 这意味着他对某事感到难过，通常是一个女人。

segments.en: Aha, okay.
So ecstatic, very, very happy.
segments.zh: 如此欣喜若狂，非常非常高兴。

segments.en: Feeling blue, very, very sad.
And well, another example of feelings, also a negative one is if you feel detached.
segments.zh: 再举一个情绪的例子，也是消极的，就是感到疏离（detached）。

segments.en: Detached.
All right.
So we know the word attach.
That means to put two things together.
segments.zh: 这意味着将两件事放在一起。

segments.en: Well, detached means to take two things apart.
segments.zh: 嗯，detached 的意思是把两样东西分开。

segments.en: Okay.
So what do you feel apart from?
Other people.
Aha, okay.
So for example, if I'm feeling detached, maybe it means that I don't feel like the people around me understand me.
segments.zh: 比如，如果我感到疏离，也许意味着我觉得周围的人不理解我。

segments.en: I don't want to talk to other people.
I'm just not feeling very social.
So for example, can you feel detached in your relationship?
segments.zh: 那么，比如，你能在恋爱关系里感到疏离吗？

segments.en: You can, and that's actually a really bad feeling because you should be happy in a relationship.
segments.zh: 你可以，这实际上是一种非常糟糕的感觉，因为你应该在一段关系中快乐。

segments.en: But when you're detached, it means that you don't really feel close to your boyfriend or girlfriend or husband or wife.
segments.zh: 但当你感到疏离时，意味着你觉得自己和男朋友、女朋友、丈夫或妻子并不亲近。

segments.en: Okay.
And we feel detached and lonely.
So if you feel lonely, that means that you feel?
segments.zh: 所以，如果你感到孤独，那就意味着你感觉到了？

segments.en: Similar to detached, lonely means that you don't feel like you can talk to anyone.
segments.zh: 和疏离类似，孤独意味着你觉得自己跟谁都说不上话。

segments.en: You feel alone.
You feel alone.
So I'm very lonely right now.
I have no one to talk to, no friends, you know, no one makes me feel good.
segments.zh: 我没有人可以交谈，没有朋友，你知道，没有人让我感觉良好。

segments.en: Okay.
So that means that you feel alone.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着你感到孤独。

segments.en: All right.
A lot of adjectives there, many different ways to describe the way that you feel.
segments.zh: 那里有很多形容词，许多不同的方式来描述你的感受。

segments.en: So let's take a listen to the dialogue again.
segments.zh: 所以让我们再听一次对话。

segments.en: Are you okay?
You seem a bit anxious.
Yeah, I'm okay.
I've been having a lot of mood swings lately.
segments.zh: 我最近情绪起伏特别大。

segments.en: I think it has to do with the pills my doctor prescribed that are causing chaos on my hormones.
segments.zh: 我想是医生开的药影响了激素，让我情绪乱了套。

segments.en: So you mean you feel ecstatic one minute and then blue the next?
segments.zh: 也就是说，你一会儿欣喜若狂，一会儿又闷闷不乐？

segments.en: Yeah, it's weird.
For example, just this morning I was feeling detached and lonely, even though there was really no reason to feel that way.
segments.zh: 就像今天早上，我无缘无故觉得跟周围格格不入，又很孤单。

segments.en: Well, maybe your mood will swing positively and you will feel confident, brave, and hopeful.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许你的心情会积极变化，你会感到自信、勇敢和充满希望。

segments.en: I hope you're right.
All right, we're back.
So now let's take a look at Fluency Builder.
Fluency Builder.
So on Fluency Builder today, the first phrase is mood swings.
segments.zh: 所以在今天的流利表达上，第一个短语是情绪波动。

segments.en: I've been having a lot of mood swings lately.
segments.zh: 我最近情绪起伏特别大。

segments.en: That's right.
So this basically means that your mood is changing constantly, all the time.
segments.zh: 所以这基本上意味着你的情绪一直在不断变化。

segments.en: That's right.
So mood is the way that you feel and to swing means to go back and forth.
segments.zh: 所以 mood 是你感受的方式，而 swing 的意思是来回摆动。

segments.en: So I'm happy, I'm sad, I'm angry, I'm lazy.
segments.zh: 所以我很高兴，我很伤心，我很生气，我很懒惰。

segments.en: So these are mood swings and it means that you're not normal, you're not flat, you're going up and down and feeling many different things.
segments.zh: 所以这些就是 mood swings，意思是你不是一成不变的，情绪有起有落，会有很多不同的感受。

segments.en: Okay.
So to be clear, also your mood is the way that you feel at a certain time or a certain day.
segments.zh: 所以说清楚，你的心情也是你在某个时间或某一天的感受。

segments.en: That's right.
So you're in a good mood today.
Did you get good news?
That's right.
So that means that you look like you are happy or it seems that your personality is positive today.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着你看起来很快乐，或者你今天的性格似乎是积极的。

segments.en: That's right.
Or you could say, I'm in a bad mood.
segments.zh: 或者你可以说，我心情不好。

segments.en: Don't talk to me.
So maybe you're angry.
Yeah.
All right.
Very good.
Now to basically explain why we're having these mood swings, we say that, well, maybe it has to do with the pills the doctor prescribed that are causing chaos on my hormones.
segments.zh: 现在要基本上解释为什么我们会出现这些情绪波动，我们说，好吧，这可能与医生开的药片有关，这些药片会导致我的荷尔蒙混乱。

segments.en: All right.
Chaos is a thing.
It's a noun.
And chaos means that there's no order.
Everything is crazy.
It's out of control.
And so basically what this person is saying is that the pills that he's taking, it can feel out of control.
segments.zh: 所以基本上这个人所说的是他正在服用的药片，可能会让人感觉失控。

segments.en: Right.
Exactly.
So they are causing chaos.
To cause chaos, to cause nothing in control and on your hormones.
segments.zh: to cause chaos，就是让一切都失控，还会紊乱你的激素。

segments.en: So, but what does hormones have to do with your mood?
segments.zh: 那么，但是荷尔蒙与你的情绪有什么关系呢？

segments.en: All right.
Hormones are chemicals that your body actually produces.
segments.zh: 激素是您的身体实际产生的化学物质。

segments.en: Women have different hormones from men, but they affect the way that we feel.
segments.zh: 女性的荷尔蒙与男性不同，但它们会影响我们的感受。

segments.en: So oftentimes you could say that I'm in a bad mood because of my hormones.
segments.zh: 所以很多时候你会说我心情不好，因为我的荷尔蒙。

segments.en: Pregnant women are very famous for having mood swings, happy, sad, angry, because they have more hormones in their bodies that they're not used to.
segments.zh: 孕妇以情绪波动、快乐、悲伤、愤怒而闻名，因为她们体内有更多不习惯的荷尔蒙。

segments.en: And so they cannot control the way that they feel.
segments.zh: 所以他们无法控制他们的感受。

segments.en: That's right.
So an example is if a man has too much of one hormone, like testosterone is a hormone, then this person will usually be very aggressive.
segments.zh: 所以一个例子是，如果一个人的激素过多，就像睾酮是一种激素一样，那么这个人通常会非常具有攻击性。

segments.en: Right?
That's right.
And the female counterpart to testosterone is estrogen.
segments.zh: 与睾酮的女性对应物是雌激素。

segments.en: So if you have too much estrogen, maybe you'll be a little bit too sensitive.
segments.zh: 所以如果你有太多的雌激素，也许你会有点太敏感了。

segments.en: Or emotional.
Or emotional.
That's right.
Okay.
So that's what we talk about chaos and hormones.
segments.zh: 这就是我们说的混乱和荷尔蒙。

segments.en: Now, when we talked about mood swings, we take it as a noun, right?
segments.zh: 现在，当我们谈到情绪波动时，我们把它当作一个名词，对吧？

segments.en: You have mood swings.
But then at the end of the dialogue, we say, well, maybe your mood will swing positively.
segments.zh: 但在对话结束时，我们会说，好吧，也许你的情绪会发生积极的变化。

segments.en: So now we're talking, it's separate.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们在谈论，它是分开的。

segments.en: It's not a noun.
We're taking swing as a verb.
To swing.
That means, think about a pendulum, you know, a clock, it goes left and then swings right.
segments.zh: 这意味着，想想一个钟摆，你知道，一个时钟，它向左然后向右摆动。

segments.en: So we could talk about a mood like this.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以谈论这样的情绪。

segments.en: So maybe your bad mood will swing the other way.
segments.zh: 所以也许你的坏心情会往另一个方向转。

segments.en: Maybe it will become a good mood.
segments.zh: 也许它会成为一种好心情。

segments.en: And so to swing here is the verb.
segments.zh: 所以在这里摇摆是动词。

segments.en: You can maybe try and encourage your mood to swing.
segments.zh: 你也许可以试着让自己的心情发生转变。

segments.en: Okay.
So to be clear, mood swings are a noun.
segments.zh: 所以说清楚，情绪波动是一个名词。

segments.en: But then in this last part, we put the verb to swing to kind of explain where mood swings comes from, right?
segments.zh: 但在这最后一部分，我们用动词摆动来解释情绪波动的来源，对吧？

segments.en: So the noun mood swings.
Now you understand that it's kind of like a pendulum and it's swinging back and forth and you're changing constantly.
segments.zh: 现在你明白它有点像钟摆，它来回摆动，你不断变化。

segments.en: Exactly.
All right.
Let's listen to the dialogue one last time.
segments.zh: 我们最后再听一遍对话。

segments.en: Are you okay?
You seem a bit anxious.
Yeah, I'm okay.
I've been having a lot of mood swings lately.
segments.zh: 我最近情绪起伏特别大。

segments.en: I think it has to do with the pills my doctor prescribed that are causing chaos on my hormones.
segments.zh: 我想是医生开的药影响了激素，让我情绪乱了套。

segments.en: So you mean you feel ecstatic one minute and then blue the next?
segments.zh: 也就是说，你一会儿欣喜若狂，一会儿又闷闷不乐？

segments.en: Yeah, it's weird.
For example, just this morning I was feeling detached and lonely.
segments.zh: 例如，就在今天早上，我感到超然和孤独。

segments.en: Even though there was really no reason to feel that way.
segments.zh: 尽管真的没有理由有这种感觉。

segments.en: Well maybe your mood will swing positively and you will feel confident, brave and hopeful.
segments.zh: 也许你的情绪会往好的方向转，变得自信、勇敢、充满希望。

segments.en: I hope you're right.
All right.
So talking about moods, now there are certain, well maybe like conditions where your mood is negatively affecting your life.
segments.zh: 说到情绪，有些……嗯，也许可以说是病症，你的情绪会对生活产生负面影响。

segments.en: Like for example, a person that suffers from anxiety.
segments.zh: 例如，一个患有焦虑症的人。

segments.en: That's right.
They have anxiety disorders and this means that they're always worried about something.
segments.zh: 他们有焦虑症，这意味着他们总是担心一些事情。

segments.en: Right.
So they're always anxious.
Always anxious.
So people who are anxious often tap their fingers or their pencils or their foot, talk quickly.
segments.zh: 所以焦虑的人常常敲手指、敲铅笔、跺脚，说话也很快。

segments.en: So anxiety, it's not fun to feel anxious and you can only imagine.
segments.zh: 所以焦虑，感到焦虑并不好玩，你只能想象。

segments.en: So a lot of times these people who have anxiety problems, they will see their psychiatrist and they will try and get some medicine, some pills to help regulate their emotions, to help them feel in control.
segments.zh: 所以很多时候，这些有焦虑问题的人会去看精神科医生，试着开一些药、一些药丸，帮助调节情绪，让自己感觉能掌控自己。

segments.en: Okay.
So that I think is the most interesting thing for me is because your mood is actually very much dependent on what's going on chemically in your body.
segments.zh: 所以我认为对我来说最有趣的事情是因为你的情绪实际上很大程度上取决于你体内发生的化学反应。

segments.en: So as you said, you could actually balance out maybe if you're feeling too anxious with drugs, you can actually make you feel less anxious because of the chemicals.
segments.zh: 所以就像你说的，如果你太焦虑，其实可以用药物来调节，因为药物里的化学成分能让你不那么焦虑。

segments.en: Exactly.
And it's also important to remember that it's not just drugs that you take.
segments.zh: 同样重要的是要记住，你服用的不仅仅是药物。

segments.en: Sometimes people like to exercise and that helps them feel relaxed and calm because when you exercise actually, your body produces certain chemicals that help you feel happy.
segments.zh: 有时人们喜欢运动，这有助于他们感到放松和平静，因为当你实际锻炼时，你的身体会产生某些化学物质，这些化学物质可以帮助你感到快乐。

segments.en: Or when you eat, sometimes when you haven't eaten, you notice that you're very, very cranky.
segments.zh: 或者说到吃，有时候你没吃东西的时候，会发现自己非常非常烦躁。

segments.en: Oh God, why are you doing this?
segments.zh: 哦，上帝，你为什么要这样做？

segments.en: Why are you being like this?
And you eat and all of a sudden, oh, your body chemistry starts to change and so you feel better.
segments.zh: 你吃东西，突然间，哦，你的身体化学物质开始改变，所以你感觉好多了。

segments.en: I heard that some people that suffer from anxiety disorders will be also compulsive eaters because they're nervous.
segments.zh: 我听说有些患有焦虑症的人因为紧张，也会变成强迫性进食者。

segments.en: So you know this, that some people eat when they're nervous.
segments.zh: 所以你知道这一点，有些人在紧张时会吃东西。

segments.en: This is one of the side effects possibly, right?
segments.zh: 这可能是副作用之一，对吧？

segments.en: It is.
segments.zh: 确实是其中一种副作用。

segments.en: I've heard this too, that a lot of people who are nervous or who are anxious, they overeat.
segments.zh: 我也听说过，很多紧张或焦虑的人，他们暴饮暴食。

segments.en: That means they eat too much.
segments.zh: 这意味着他们吃得太多了。

segments.en: Even when they're not hungry.
Even when they're not hungry.
And this actually has a very large effect on your body because obviously, like I said, your body chemistry affects your mood.
segments.zh: 这实际上对你的身体有很大的影响，因为很明显，就像我说的，你的身体化学物质会影响你的情绪。

segments.en: So if you eat too much, your body maybe reacts negatively and you're even less happy.
segments.zh: 因此，如果你吃得太多，你的身体可能会产生负面反应，你就更不开心了。

segments.en: It happens to me sometimes in the movie theater, like a really good scene or I'm nervous or there's an action sequence and I'm just eating that popcorn up and I'm already really, really thirsty but I just can't stop.
segments.zh: 我有时在电影院就会这样，比如看到一个很精彩的场景，或者我很紧张，或者有动作场面，我就一直吃爆米花，明明已经很渴了，可就是停不下来。

segments.en: That's funny.
So if you have any questions or any other ways to describe feelings, maybe you could post them on our boards at EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 所以如果你有任何问题，或者有其他描述感受的说法，也许可以发到我们 EnglishPod.com 的论坛上。

segments.en: There are so many different feelings and most of them have words or names.
segments.zh: 有很多不同的感觉，其中大多数都有单词或名字。

segments.en: Look those up in your dictionaries and let us know.
segments.zh: 在您的字典中查找这些并告诉我们。

segments.en: All right.
We'll see you guys there.
Bye.
